messages:
maria: Heads-up — saw a recurring latency bump on our PP 8x8 job with 1F1B when microbatch=8. Not consistent but ~10% of iterations spike by ~20-40ms.
sam: Can you paste the flame or the perf summary? is it all-reduce or compute stall?
maria: quick profile snippet from the run:
```
[pp-step 42] compute: 120ms | allreduce-wait: 45ms | kv-reload: 30ms | idle: 5ms
[pp-step 43] compute: 118ms | allreduce-wait: 200ms | kv-reload: 28ms | idle: 3ms
```
maria: notice the allreduce-wait jump correlates w/ KV cache re-pop events (we see small batch alignment changes).
jonathan: hmmm — kernel selection could be flipping when sequence-length distribution changes between microbatches. If kernel switches, it can add jitter and force more synchronization.
li: also check NCCL tuning + collectives scheduling. 1F1B exposes more frequent cross-rank barriers when microbatching is small.
sam: what’s the microbatch timeline? are we queuing uneven prefixes across PP stages?
maria: microbatch order is contiguous; but prefix KV hits depend on token length per request, so stage 2 sometimes receives an earlier-than-expected hot cache miss and does an extra load.
jonathan: two things to try: (1) sticky kernel selection per-model-version for a window (avoid per-microbatch flip), (2) aggregate microbatch boundaries so allreduce aligns to the same offsets.
perf-bot: perf alert created: TICKET-3456. Attached perf traces: https://perf.internal/runs/1780601234
sam: also saw in other repros that when kv-reload happens it stalls the compute stream and NCCL enqueues pile up -> allreduce stalls. Maybe move KV loads to a higher-priority stream or prefetch into GPU memory earlier.
li: we can try async KV prefetch + grant it higher cuda stream priority and see if allreduce wait disappears. also check ncclAsyncMode flags.
maria: schedule for a quick experiment: try microbatch=4 vs 8, sticky-kernel window=200ms, and async prefetch toggled. will run tonight and post traces.
jonathan: if this shows improvement, we should add a heuristic: if kv-reload rate > X, reduce microbatch by 2 or enable prefetch automatically.
sam: +1. also add a per-stage counter for kernel-switch events to the console dashboard. :eyes:
li: noted. will instrument and add a counter metric and an alert if allreduce-wait > 150ms more than 2% in a minute.
maria: thanks team — will drop results and perf links here tomorrow. :thumbsup:
